drivers: one small team and one release cadence
strong consistency between slots, bookings, payments and the waiting list (no double booking, no charge without booking)
modest scale with no part needing independent scaling
BookNow, the only source with code, is Python

alternatives.reason: splitting bookings from payments and the waiting list would turn the single-transaction hold-charge-confirm flow into a distributed saga with no scaling benefit
the waiting list reacts to a freed slot asynchronously, but one in-process event covers it without a message broker
there is no existing system that must stay separate; Stripe is called through its SDK
a monolith plus a broker for slot-freed would work but adds infrastructure the volume does not justify; revisit if calendar sync (M07) is added

style.reason: The simplest design that keeps booking, payment and waiting-list state consistent in one database transaction; the one asynchronous reaction (slot freed -> waitlist offer) is an in-process event plus a scheduled job for offer expiry.

stack.frontend: Django templates (server-rendered) with htmx for small partial updates
stack.backend: Python 3.12, Django 5 (LTS line), Stripe Python SDK in test mode during development
stack.jobs: Django management command run every minute by the host's scheduler (offer expiry)
stack.hosting: a managed Python host plus managed PostgreSQL, chosen by the user; no deployment in this run

reasons.frontend: D10: no source has a UI to reuse and the app is form-and-list heavy; server rendering keeps one codebase and works with session cookies
reasons.backend: D10: BookNow's logic is Python; Django brings auth, sessions, CSRF, admin and migrations, which neither source provides
reasons.database: D11: partial unique indexes and transactions enforce one active booking per slot (D06); timestamps with time zone
reasons.jobs: D12: offer expiry needs a timer; a scheduled command avoids a queue broker
reasons.hosting: D13: no hosting constraint given; deployment is out of scope and never automatic

modules.name: accounts
modules.responsibility: sign-up, sign-in, sessions, roles and the single permission check used by every route and query

modules.name: slots
modules.responsibility: staff create, publish, edit and withdraw slots; customers list open slots

modules.name: payments
modules.responsibility: Stripe charges with idempotency keys, refunds, and the Stripe webhook

modules.name: bookings
modules.responsibility: hold-charge-confirm booking of one slot, 24-hour cancellation with refund, and the slot-freed event

modules.name: recurring
modules.responsibility: weekly series of 2 to 12 bookings, all-or-nothing creation and series cancellation

modules.name: waitlist
modules.responsibility: join and leave a slot's waiting list; offer freed places in join order with a time-limited hold

entities.name: User
entities.notes: Neither source has accounts; A's user_id becomes a foreign key to this table (D07)

entities.name: Slot
entities.notes: A's taken flag is not stored: 'taken' is derived from an active booking, enforced by a partial unique index on Booking (D06, D09)

entities.name: Booking
entities.notes: Soft cancel (D02); status held | confirmed | cancelled; series_id replaces B's 'recurring' option (D08)

entities.name: BookingSeries
entities.notes: Weekly recurrence of 2 to 12 occurrences (B rule recurrence_max_weeks = 12)

entities.name: Payment
entities.notes: A's payments module was not provided, so this is designed fresh (D01, D02)

entities.name: WaitlistEntry
entities.notes: status waiting | offered | accepted | expired | left; one offer at a time per slot (D03)
